brief_summary:
To compare the efficacy of fixed-dose versus treat-to-target statin regimens in achieving the predefined LDL-C target at 12 weeks in patients with established ASCVD.

To compare the frequency of adverse effects of statin therapy between patients receiving a fixed-dose regimen and those managed with a treat-to-target approach.
brief_title: Effectiveness and Tolerability of a Treat-to-Target Versus Fixed-Dose Statin Strategy in Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* adults aged between 18 to 80 years requiring primary prevention or those with history of at least 1 episode of ASCVD
* who are either statin-naïve or already on statins but not at target LDL-C levels and are eligible for dose adjustment.

Exclusion Criteria:

* have already achieved target LDL-C levels on a high-dose statin and tolerate it well
* have contraindications to statin therapy such as active liver disease or severe renal impairment (eGFR \< 30 mL/min/1.73m²)
* have known hypersensitivity or a prior life-threatening reaction to any statin
* are pregnant or lactating
* are using other lipid-lowering agents like ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, fibrates, or bile acid sequestrants.

official_title: Effectiveness and Tolerability of a Treat-to-Target Versus Fixed-Dose Statin Strategy in Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial
